subject: Example for handling a Non-Stationary field

messages.author: de3b975379e58e58
messages.subject: Example for handling a Non-Stationary field
parts:
Hello,
         I am using R-INLA to infer distributional parameters, given high dimensional spatial data. I then use the inferred distribution to generate more samples of the underlying field. I am new to R-INLA and spatial statistics in general, so please excuse any gross errors/missteps. 

I did a trial run with a subset of the data, assuming stationarity. Everything checked out in that case, and I now want to move to the non-stationary case.

I have been following the reference 'Bayesian Spatial Modelling with R-INLA' so far, specifically sections 2.1 - 2.6. However, I have not been able to locate an equivalent example for the non-stationary case. I would be grateful if someone could point me to some examples that handle non-stationarity.

Regards.

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Example for handling a Non-Stationary field
parts:
Have you seen the SPDE-tutorial?

This contains several examples; I don't remember if it has a non-stationary example, but you can check.

Otherwise, papers by Rikke Ingebrigtsen and Geir-Arne Fuglstad may have INLA code in supplementary material.

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
